findings.text: gate lot-7/lock:spring-hall: G7 minus levy {wallJump, dash, doubleJump, pogo, seize} bypasses it; minimal: {wallJump, seize} or {doubleJump, seize}
findings.accepted: Known since the L3 audit (item 3): with Wall Jump or Double Jump (plus Seize) the upper corridor is reached without the pink spring. Harmless today because Lot 7 SETS abilities on entry (gym semantics: the gate holds against {seize}); it becomes real once abilities persist (Phase 3). world-design.md rebuilds this as B2 (teachGate) + B3 (sealed plate door).

findings.text: gate yard/lock:bar-wall: room kit {dash, seize, levy} without the seize:up aim bypasses it
findings.accepted: Found at the L4 merge by the new aim check: the Yard's section B is meant to teach Up+Seize (bar 1 overhead), but a forward Seize at the top of a running jump also takes the bar (the fwd box [28,8,64,72] reaches ~15 px into it at the apex), after which the wall spring works as intended. Evidence: tests/replays/yard-bar-wall.fwd-seize.json. Left for the combat/level owner: raising the bar one tile makes the forward seize miss but leaves Up+Seize only a ~7 px window at the apex, so the fix is a design call (bar height vs seize boxes). Section C (Down+Levy to the G ledge) holds: no forward/up/neutral levy reached G in a 9.7k-timing sweep (control with Down+Levy: 22 hits in 2.4k).
